title.value: THE JOURNEY MATTERS: AVERAGE PARAMETER COUNT OVER PRE-TRAINING UNIFIES SPARSE AND DENSE SCALING LAWS
title.justification: The title of the paper captures the main idea explored in the research, which is about unifying sparse and dense scaling laws through average parameter count over pre-training.
title.quote: T HE J OURNEY M ATTERS : A VERAGE P ARAMETER C OUNT OVER P RE - TRAINING U NIFIES S PARSE AND D ENSE S CALING L AWS

analysis.description: This paper explores the optimal configurations for sparse pre-training of large language models (LLMs), revealing that initiating pruning at 25% and concluding at 75% of the total training compute achieves near-optimal evaluation loss. It proposes a scaling law that uses average parameter count during pre-training to model evaluation loss for both sparse and dense LLMs, offering computational savings by maintaining model quality while reducing model size.

type.justification: The paper presents empirical results from testing over 80 configurations of sparse pre-training schedules and validates the proposed scaling laws through empirical data and experiments.
type.quote: To validate this approach, we evaluate over 80 combinations of sparse pre-training schedules, sparsity levels, and training durations.

name.justification: The paper focuses on adapting pre-training techniques for large language models, which is a core area of research in natural language processing.
name.quote: Sparse pre-training integrates neural network pruning into pre-training and offers a promising solution to these challenges by activating only a subset of parameters during both training and inference, reducing computational costs; it gained prominence when Lottery Ticket Hypothesis presented compelling evidence for its feasibility.

name.justification: The paper discusses various techniques related to neural network pruning, specifically for large language models, and how they relate to sparse and dense scaling laws.
name.quote: Pruning eliminates unnecessary parameters in neural networks; it offers a promising solution to the growing computational demands of large language models (LLMs).

name.justification: The paper presents a new scaling law that incorporates average parameter count to unify sparse and dense scaling laws for LLMs, highlighting its importance in the research.
name.quote: We unify sparse and dense scaling laws by modifying the parameter count term in the Chinchilla model and extending it to model sparse pre-training.

name.justification: The paper explicitly mentions using the LLaMA 2 base model architecture for training large language models during experiments.
name.quote: We use the LLaMA 2 base model architecture.

is_contributed.justification: The paper uses LLaMA 2 as a baseline and does not claim any modifications or contributions to this model.
is_contributed.quote: For each unique model size, we train two versions: one using over 10x the number of tokens corresponding to Chinchilla optimal, and the other using over 20x Chinchilla optimal. We train substantially past Chinchilla-optimal dataset size, following prevailing practice.

is_executed.justification: The paper describes experiments conducted with the LLaMA 2 model on hardware such as TPUv4 and TPUv5, indicating that the model was executed.
is_executed.quote: Software and hardware. Our work uses TPUv4 and TPUv5 hardware for training LLMs. We modify MaxText to support sparse pre-training of LLMs.

is_compared.justification: The LLaMA 2 models are used in comparisons as the paper examines sparse versus dense pre-training configurations to evaluate model performance.
is_compared.quote: In Figure 1, we demonstrated that sparse and dense pre-training runs, starting with 138 million prunable parameters models and matching average parameter counts, achieve similar perplexity.
